intents.title: The founder's return report: what happened while he was away, from the ledger alone
intents.statement: "You disappear from operational involvement for several days. When you return, UNIIMENTE does not merely tell you, 'I completed 842 tasks'. It tells you: Three authorized missions remained active [...] $18,430 moved through authorized budgets; every movement reconciled. Two actions were blocked by policy. One decision exceeds delegated authority and is waiting for you. Here are the receipts, causal evidence, failures, financial results, and what the institution learned." (founder-voiced, Material 7). Compiled effect: a deterministic, idempotent, ledger-derived digest over a time window that separates executed (with receipts) from prepared, Gate refusals from classifier withholding, unknown attempts awaiting reconciliation, decisions waiting as of the window end, declared cost estimates (never settlement) with reconciliation flags, retained assets, and what changed in the world model; it is information and requests nothing.
intents.source: Founder-supplied material in Claude Code cloud session session_01TnTfFXr93jtNSzVD9SWeGx, 2026-10-14 (chat text is lineage, not founder authentication)
intents.source_location: docs/intent/sources/EGREGORE-SYNTHESIS-MATERIALS-2026-10-14-source.md, Material 7 "At full intended maturity", the paragraph beginning "The scene that would convince me"
intents.intended_outcome: After any absence the founder reads one report, folded from ledger records with logical time inside the window, in which no prepared move is counted as executed, no executor claim is counted as verification, no estimate is presented as money moved, and nothing is requested; two loops over one ledger or one loop across a restart produce the same report; recording it twice appends nothing.
affected_systems: uniimente-kernel egregore/gravity.py (GoalGravityLoop.return_report; the prior-attempt guard the report's tests exposed)
uniimente-kernel egregore/closure.py (evidence closure asserts the report is ledger-derived information)
intents.rationale: Draft PR #160 implemented targets A-I with per-goal status() and global measures() but no cross-goal, time-windowed digest; the founder's own acceptance scene is exactly that digest. Building it as a read-only fold of the existing records adds no authority object and reuses every record the loop, Gate, attention router and retention already write.
conflicts: The scene's figures ('$18,430 moved', 'closed one paying customer') describe settlement and commercial closure that no Kernel ledger today records; the report therefore labels money as declared estimates with reconciliation flags and says so, rather than inventing a settlement column

While building the report's tests a defect in draft #160 was reproduced (a grantless wake re-classified a route with an open attempt and later allowed a second dispatch); fixed in this increment with regression tests (tests/evidence/goal-gravity-20261013/defect-repro-increment-4.log)
evidence_refs: Evidence tier: IMPLEMENTED, UNIT-TESTED, INTEGRATION-TESTED on synthetic ledgers; not SANDBOX-VERIFIED, not EXTERNALLY VERIFIED, not FOUNDER-ACCEPTED

intents.title: A host-owned trigger discovers due work without a human tick (wake schedule view)
intents.statement: Directive section 3: "Design appropriate: dormant states; wake conditions; event triggers; priority queues; resource ceilings; relevance thresholds; review cadences; urgency classes. A long-horizon objective may sleep for months. A relevant event may wake it instantly." Founder-loop entry gate P1: "a bounded host-owned trigger discovers it without a human tick". Compiled effect: a read-only view of every cadence due time and every deferred ask's resurface time, the earliest of them, and a stable trigger id for it, so that whichever scheduler the founder selects (G5) can call turn() at the right moment.
intents.source: Goal Gravity directive (third issuance) and docs/founder-loop-entry-gate.json G5/P1
intents.source_location: docs/intent/sources/GOAL-GRAVITY-DIRECTIVE-2026-10-13-source.md section 3 and section 24 C; docs/founder-loop-entry-gate.json entries G5 and P1
intents.intended_outcome: Any host scheduler can compute, from durable state alone, when to next call turn() and with which trigger id; the view appends nothing and runs nothing; paused, revoked, superseded, completed and awake goals are never scheduled; a turn at the computed time wakes exactly the due goal by cadence.
intents.rationale: G5 forbids a new scheduler before founder selection; the view is the interface every candidate (cron, APScheduler as DALEOBANKS runs, Temporal) needs and is the smallest mechanism that makes P1 testable without building a trigger component.
conflicts: G5 remains DECISION_REQUIRED_BEFORE_NEW_ARCHITECTURE; this record does not select a scheduler and the gate file is unchanged
Material 6 proposes Temporal plus LangGraph as the substrate; recorded separately as INTENT-20261014-durable-execution-substrate (exploratory)
evidence_refs: Evidence tier: IMPLEMENTED, UNIT-TESTED; no host scheduler has called turn() on its own clock
intents.owner: alfonso_lopez (G5 selection); Kernel egregore maintainers implement
intents.next_review_trigger: Founder selects the bounded host trigger (G5); first scheduler integration
unresolved_questions: Which scheduler owns the trigger clock (G5)?

intents.title: Content-addressed causal memory with branchable, auditable history ("Git-native DAG for cognition")
intents.statement: Materials 1 and 3 ask for "a Git-native causal Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG) for all internal state management", content-addressed blobs/trees/commits, branch-and-merge of parallel realities, "the log itself is the history", local hydration into a read model, deterministic topological sorting in compiled code, and causal ancestry/descendant/counterfactual queries. Compiled effect: every consequential record is immutable, content-addressed and linked by provenance; contradictions coexist until resolved by a record; failures are preserved; the institution can reconstruct how it reached any state and ask what caused what.
intents.source_location: docs/intent/sources/EGREGORE-SYNTHESIS-MATERIALS-2026-10-14-source.md, Material 1 ("Theoretical Framework III") and Material 3 (whole essay)
intents.intended_outcome: Immutable, hash-linked, content-addressed institutional records with causal links and preserved contradictions, hydrated into in-memory projections for cheap reads, with deterministic dependency ordering computed in code rather than by a model.
affected_systems: uniimente-kernel provenance/ledger.py (append-only hash chain; corrections point at the record they correct)
uniimente-kernel egregore/* (content-derived identifiers; every projection is a fold of the ledger)
intents.rationale: The effect already exists on main: EvidenceLedger is an append-only SHA-256 chain anchored to the constitution, CausalMemory walks causal_parent links, egregore identifiers are content digests, the twins package runs counterfactual forks that recommend and never apply, and the Goal Gravity projections hydrate from records. A literal Git object model, a rewritten Git server, Entire/KoruDelta-style forges, CRDT merges and grammar-constrained decoding are mechanism research, not requirements; INTENT-0030 regresses the literal framing and the Technology Map itself downgrades the Git port to 'ceremony over real Git'.
conflicts: Material 3's roadmap (Epochs 1-5, 2026-2035) and throughput figures (570,000 clones/hour) are forecasts and vendor claims, not requirements; recorded as exploratory
Material 4 asks for a git commit after every decision; the hash chain already yields rollback and audit without Git, so the commit is optional tooling, not a requirement
evidence_refs: provenance/ledger.py::verify_chain and tests/unit (full suite green on this branch)
egregore/absence.py (a fold of records; identical across two loops and a restart)
Mechanisms cited by the essays (Gitlet, pygit, Dolt, KoruDelta, Beads, AgentReplay, Entire) are unverified external references in this record
intents.owner: Kernel provenance/memory maintainers; alfonso_lopez for any literal-substrate decision
intents.next_review_trigger: A measured ledger-growth or branching problem that the current chain and projections cannot serve; or a founder instruction that the Git object model itself is a requirement
unresolved_questions: Is a materialized read model (SQLite) needed before 24/7 operation, and at what ledger size?
Should counterfactual branches (twins/) be fed from Goal Gravity goal records?

intents.title: Substrate sovereignty: 'what I cannot create, I do not understand' versus acquire-before-inventing
intents.statement: Materials 1, 3 and 5 assert that "If an AI relies on external APIs, opaque libraries, or black-box systems for its cognitive operations, it is not autonomous", that the system "will never rely on assumed external infrastructure or black-box APIs for its core cognitive functions", and that databases, blockchains, containers, operating systems, network stacks and neural networks should be built from scratch. Compiled effect: the founder owns, pins, exports and can replay the law, history and capability registry that decide institutional outcomes; no vendor change alters a verdict; the institution survives any provider; commodity mechanics are rented, the control plane is owned.
intents.source: Founder-forwarded AI-generated essays supplied 2026-10-14 (Materials 1, 3, 5) read against the Technology Map PDF and Kernel doctrine
intents.source_location: docs/intent/sources/EGREGORE-SYNTHESIS-MATERIALS-2026-10-14-source.md, Material 1 ("Theoretical Framework II", Layer 2 of the Master System Prompt), Material 3, Material 5; Technology Map PDF (sha256 036ff76f...) pages 1, 4-7, 14-17
intents.intended_outcome: Vendor independence and replayable, owned decision logic (the effect) without rebuilding commodity technology (the literal reading): deterministic constitutional evaluation owned in this repository, exportable signed records, replaceable models behind a router, and rebuild-from-ledger drills.
intents.rationale: The literal reading conflicts with three binding sources: the resourcefulness ladder (existing capability -> composition -> commodity -> open source -> ... -> new architecture), INTENT-20260930 open-source-first, and the Technology Map's own 'study only; adopt mature infrastructure' verdict with explicit rejections of a general database, Git rewrite, own neural network and browser/OS builds. The effect is already partly realized (owned UCL compiler and Gate, hash-chained ledger, model router doctrine). Both readings are preserved; the literal one is regressed per INTENT-0030's default decision.
conflicts: Material 1 Layer 2.1 'never rely on ... black-box APIs' versus INTENT-20260930 open-source-first and the Technology Map's adopt list (PostgreSQL, Git, Docker/Firecracker, mTLS, frontier LLM APIs behind a router)

Technology Map p17 'no third-party policy engines (no OPA/Rego/CEL)' versus Reality Compiler Blueprint p3-4 'OPA ... Cedar' adapters; main already carries an owned UCL compiler, which satisfies the Technology Map position without excluding adapters

Technology Map p9 relays 'You said keep the crypto' (tamper-evidence, signatures, anchoring) versus the Blueprint's adopt-Sigstore/in-toto/SLSA; the Kernel owns hash chains and a witness signer today; external anchoring is unbuilt
evidence_refs: compiler/ucl_compiler.py and policy/engine.py on main (deterministic evaluation owned in-repo)
Technology Map PDF pages 1, 4-7, 14-17 (AI-generated; verdict 'Validate', one metric, 30-day review)
intents.next_review_trigger: One founder answer: does 'sovereign' mean (a) owned, pinned, replayable decision code and exportable records, or (b) no third-party component anywhere in the decision path? (a) is current doctrine; (b) would supersede INTENT-20260930 and must be ruled explicitly
unresolved_questions: Scope of 'keep the crypto': tamper-evidence, signatures and external anchoring only (not tokens or chains)?
Must the implementation be owned code, or does adopting transparency-log tooling satisfy the effect?

intents.title: Durable execution and state persistence for endless operation (Temporal, LangGraph, APScheduler as candidates)
intents.statement: Material 6: "An autonomous entity cannot compound its successes if its cognitive processes are tethered to the ephemeral lifespan of a single hardware process"; proposes Temporal.io durable workflows with timer-based zero-cost waits and continue-as-new, LangGraph checkpointers (Postgres/Redis) and cross-thread stores. Compiled effect: a goal or workflow interrupted at any point resumes from durable state without duplicate consequential action; waiting costs nothing; a host clock, not a human, fires the next step.
intents.intended_outcome: The effect list is the contract: pause/resume/retry/reconcile, crash-after-dispatch recovery without blind retry, idempotent delivery, causal ordering, zero-cost waits and a host-owned clock; the transport and scheduler stay behind the existing organ-neutral interfaces (events/spine.py, GoalGravityLoop.turn trigger ids, WakeSchedule).
affected_systems: uniimente-kernel egregore/gravity.py (idempotent trigger ids; attempted/unknown states; reconcile)
intents.rationale: Most of the effect exists on main (DurableWorkflow checkpoints and resume refuse blind retry; the Goal Gravity loop survives SIGKILL across process images in tests). What is missing is the host clock (G5) and any supervisor. Temporal and APScheduler are mature candidates; the founder selects. LangGraph's checkpointer/store roles are already played by the ledger and its folds.
conflicts: G5 requires the founder to select a bounded trigger/supervision implementation before any new component; this record selects nothing

Technology Map proposes a Postgres-backed workflow engine and rejects brokers until throughput pain; the Blueprint proposes Temporal and NATS/Kafka; UNIIMENTE_FINAL_BUILD_ORDER section 4.9 keeps transport behind an organ-neutral interface, which accommodates both
evidence_refs: No Temporal, LangGraph or APScheduler integration exists in this repository
intents.next_review_trigger: Founder G5 selection; first scheduler integration test in which a host clock calls turn() without a human
unresolved_questions: Cron, APScheduler (as DALEOBANKS runs) or Temporal for the first host clock?

intents.title: The minimum viable continuous loop: Read State, Route, Propose, Gate, Execute, Measure, Branch on Failure
intents.statement: Material 4 asks for an event-sourced causal substrate (append-only JSONL plus a commit per decision), a deterministic orchestrator that 'does not use AI; it uses pure deterministic logic to manage the AI' with the Consequence Gate between proposal and effect, specialized single-purpose 'cellular' agents in isolated containers, a failure-driven compounding loop that isolates failures and merges verified fixes, and measurement against external reality with a Capability Genome Registry.
intents.intended_outcome: A 24/7 loop in which durable state is read, moves are classified deterministically, a model only proposes, the Gate alone executes, outcomes are measured against reality and failures become preserved evidence that improves the next cycle.
affected_systems: uniimente-kernel egregore/gravity.py (deterministic turn; model-free classification; Gate-only execution)
uniimente-kernel capabilities/genome.py and egregore/retention.py (registry; retention after verified outcomes)
intents.rationale: Four of the five steps exist on this branch in bounded form: the JSONL ledger, the deterministic loop with Gate-only execution, capability genomes with authority envelopes, and retention/evolution under ratification. Residual: a host clock (G5), an isolation facility for untrusted candidates, and any real externally verified outcome. A git commit per decision is unnecessary given the hash chain; failure 'branches' compile to preserved failed records plus ChangeProposals, not Git branches.
conflicts: Material 4's orchestrator 'executes it only if it passes all automated tests' versus the Gate's requirement of a pre-existing grant, policy and commit-time revalidation; tests are necessary, not sufficient
Isolation ('isolated Docker container') is a stated requirement with no facility in this repository (SR001 isolated verification facility blocker)
intents.next_review_trigger: G5 scheduler selection and the first host-driven turn; first externally verified outcome
unresolved_questions: Which isolation facility (container with egress allow-list, WASI, microVM) qualifies untrusted candidates first?

intents.title: The ten capabilities of UNIIMENTE at full intended maturity (founder-voiced destination)
intents.statement: Material 7 lists ten capabilities that 'should actually impress you': (1) command outcomes, not tasks; (2) discover a missing part of itself and build a replacement; (3) almost every component can die without killing UNIIMENTE; (4) run a conglomerate while the founder operates as owner/CEO; (5) turn intelligence into money or prove the idea failed; (6) temporary organizations recruited around a mission; (7) different kinds of intelligence for different problem geometries; (8) rehearse futures before spending; (9) the public media organ changes the environment future inventions need; (10) success makes the people and systems around it stronger. It closes: "it still would not need to be conscious or biologically alive".
intents.intended_outcome: Each capability is preserved as a serious destination with its current evidence state: (1) PARTIAL (goal intake, GPS, Gate-only execution; no standing grants); (2) PARTIAL (deficit detection, acquisition plan, qualification, founder-gated attach; no builder, no isolation); (3) PARTIAL (ledger continuity, replaceable models doctrine; no rebuild drill, no succession); (4) MISSING (no venture cell runs; organs proposal-only); (5) PARTIAL (reconciliation and independent verification exist; zero payments); (6) PARTIAL (OMNIMORPH manifests PROPOSED_NOT_EXECUTED); (7) PARTIAL (router by epistemic method; developmental research sealed); (8) PARTIAL (twins recommend only); (9) MISSING (no DALEOBANKS live transport); (10) MISSING (no participants yet).
affected_systems: DALEOBANKS, WealthMachineIntelligence, PumpStation organs (4, 9, 10) - unchanged by this record
intents.rationale: The founder states the destination explicitly as not-yet-achieved ('The current project is still embryonic and fragmented'). Recording each capability with its evidence state prevents 'not implemented' from becoming 'not intended' and gives every future increment a place to attach.
conflicts: Capability (4) and (9) require live organ transport and venture cells that the founder-loop entry gate holds; no build session can supply them
Capability (2)'s 'generate materially different replacement mechanisms' needs a builder lineage (#129, #164, #137) or a coding-agent route under the Capability Genesis contract; none is adopted
evidence_refs: docs/GOAL_GRAVITY.md section 4 (preserved future targets with blockers)
intents.next_review_trigger: Each founder ruling on a blocker: scheduler (G5), authentication (G6), builder lineage, live organ transport, standing grants

intents.title: PDF: '03 UNIIMENTE Reality Compiler Blueprint' (ChatGPT-generated advisory)
intents.statement: A 21-page ChatGPT-authored blueprint: treat build-your-own-x as a technology anatomy atlas; do not build a generic agent platform, custom LLM, blockchain or AI OS; build a 'proof-to-consequence compiler' of seven pieces (Institutional ISA/Reality Compiler, Reality Git, Capability Cell Runtime, Consequence Engine, Precedent Engine, Proof Credential Fabric, Capability Genome Foundry) as a thin control plane over open standards (Git/IPFS, OPA, Cedar, WASI/Wasmtime, Firecracker, SPIFFE, Temporal, in-toto, SLSA, Sigstore/Rekor, W3C VC); the first bottleneck is a named external stakeholder pre-committing to acceptance criteria; 'egregore' means 'a standing institutional process with persistent memory, bounded organs, externally legible identity, and an evidence-to-settlement metabolism', 'not an emergent consciousness'.
intents.source: Founder upload 2026-10-14; document carries a ChatGPT header and states the kernel repository returned 404 to it
intents.source_location: Upload 444d13e9-03-UNIIMENTE-Reality-Compiler-Blueprint.pdf, 21 pages, sha256 f53a255529ee97859980b51d39672c5450505439b0d3dc141ef1d555417521f8 (not copied into the repository)
intents.intended_outcome: Its de-literalization of 'egregore' and its consequence lifecycle (proposed -> evidence_ready -> policy_approved -> human_approved -> capability_issued -> commit_revalidated -> executed -> receipt_captured -> reconciled -> outcome_verified -> precedent_updated) are available as mechanism sources; its R0/R1 maturity ratings describe the model's proposal, never the kernel's state.
affected_systems: uniimente-kernel policy/consequence_gate.py (lifecycle largely realized: witness, grant, commit revalidation, receipt, outcome)
intents.rationale: The document never saw the kernel (404), so none of its state claims apply; its design direction matches main's Gate lifecycle closely and its stakeholder-first bottleneck is a serious alternative to the other two documents' first bottlenecks. All example identifiers and credentials in it are illustrative.
conflicts: First bottleneck: external stakeholder pre-commitment (this document) versus executable law (Technology Map) versus gate vertical slice (Final Plan)
'55 technologies' listed as 57 (unreviewed generation)
OPA/Cedar adapters versus the Technology Map's prohibition (see INTENT-20261014-substrate-sovereignty)
